description: Wako leg remesh + toe flip, round 3: before (original upload Wako.blend), rev2 (previous round) and after (game/LogicObjects/Wako/Wako.blend rebuilt by pipeline/wako_mesh_rebuild.py revision 3)

summary.whole_mesh_symmetry_error_m_note: the whole-mesh error comes from the untouched original body; legs are mirrored exactly
summary.per_leg_loops: 4 hip + 1 thigh + 9 knee fan + 1 shin + 8 ankle + 2 foot + 3 sole-rim rings (16 sides), all-quad 8->16 junction, 4x4 sole patch

leg_face_quality_note: after: 936 leg quads, no triangles. Corners < 25 deg (19.6) are the side quads of the 8->16 junction transition row directly under the body flange (row moved closer to the flange to remove a visible fold at hip 120 + spread 30); every sole cell is now 39-143 deg (the inner sole rim is a squarer superellipse, so the 4x4 patch has no 160-173 deg corner cells).

godot_import_check.note: 7 non-toe bone rests identical (0 deviation); toe rests changed by the 180 deg flip (origin (0, 0.056, -0.06), pointing along Godot -Z = runtime forward). 34 animations, same names; 1 surface; skin with 9 binds; tangents + UV; albedo found via the relative texture path (the original's absolute Windows path does not resolve).

profile_line_checks.method: pipeline/wako_deform_metrics.py 'lines': sagittal polyline of the left leg's front (or back) column (|x+0.237| < 0.012), per-vertex turn of the posed line in the YZ plane (turn_abs = exactly the review's knee_profile measure; turn_change = minus the rest-line turn, so designed rest curvature such as the rounded sole edge is not counted) and segment stretch posed/rest. Knee band rest z 0.22-0.66; ankle band z 0.0-0.30; toe outline = the toe-side column below z 0.20 continued along the sole centre (the original rig's toe is at the BACK, so its outline uses the back column).
profile_line_checks.targets_from_review: knee 145: no front vertex turns more than ~15-20 deg, no segment stretches more than ~2x

hip_socket_depth_cm_mean_p90_numpy.method: rays from below / below-rear / below-front through the body junction opening; depth of the first leg surface beyond the junction plane (left leg; numpy LBS of the exact skin matrices)
hip_socket_depth_cm_mean_p90_numpy.crater_free_limit: after: <= 0.11 / 0.36 cm up to hip 100 deg (knee 90); 0.43 / 1.75 cm at the flip tuck (hip 110); 1.56 / 4.44 cm at the hip-120 ground-seated stress pose

junction_numpy.note: max dihedral counts only edges outside the body hull; the original junction looks 'clean' in the tuck only because its thigh cut ~3100 cm2 into the body

two_d_optimisation.knee: front line of 9 fan loops (s = +11.6 ... -9.4 cm, weights 0.043 ... 0.954, rigid thigh/shin ends) optimised for 60/90/120/145 deg: predicted max turn 17.2 deg, stretch 1.86 at 145
two_d_optimisation.ankle: 8 loops z 0.198 ... 0.059 with weights 0.16 ... 0.90 optimised so the front never folds back (dorsi up to 60) and the back never folds back (plantar 35); predicted max turn 16-26 deg

notes.hip_limit: the hip joint sits 11 cm above the body bottom: at 110-120 deg flexion the upper thigh is inside the rigid body and leaves through its front face, so any skin joining the fixed junction ring to it dips into the body (linear blend skinning, no helper bone or corrective shape, which Godot drops under the current import settings). The slow-behind hip weights halve the visible depth at hip 110 versus rev2; up to hip ~100 there is no socket. Recommended: keep runtime hip flexion <= ~95-100 deg in the tuck and add the rest as body pitch, or allow a hip helper bone / lower hip pivot in a later round.
notes.runtime_tuck_today: wako_head_leap.gd _stunt_leg_points lifts the ankle target 0.30 m up (0.045 m back) with a forward knee pole: with thigh 0.41 / shin 0.399 that is about hip 45 deg / knee 102 deg at full tuck, well inside the socket-free range
notes.ankle_fold: at 45-60 deg flat-sole dorsiflexion the shin front (11.5 cm in front of the ankle hinge) must pass over the foot front; the broad blend turns this into one smooth rounded fold instead of the rev2 wedge/crumple (front turn change 81 -> 20 deg at crouch 90)
notes.toe_folds: a +-45 deg toe rotation about an axis 5.5 cm behind the front face and 5.6 cm above the sole must fold ~4 cm of surface: -45 forms one rounded crease above the lifted pad, +45 one crease under the pad (plantar). Standing +45 still sinks below the floor, as any toe curled into the ground would.

toe_animation_check.method: 33 actions evaluated at 7 frames each in the original and rebuilt files; toe tail displacement relative to the foot, projected on the toe's own pointing direction and on world up
toe_animation_check.conclusion: the flip is a rigid Rz(pi) pre-multiply of the rest frame: local-X rotation keys still curl/lift the tip in the same sense along the toe, local-Y location keys still retract along it; the existing toe channels are NOT reversed and re-authoring must not invert them

runtime_toe_frame_consumers: wako_helper.gd:1336-1337, 1359-1361, 1380 -- tool anchor basis built from toe.basis.x / toe.basis.y; grip = toe.origin + toe.basis.y*0.035; tool tip along toe.basis.y
wako_pose.gd:496-500, 529 -- foot-held grip offset toe.basis.y*0.035 in the foot frame; :1850 aligns toe.basis.y to the work axis

wako_back_tool.gd:437-540, 654, 752, 848-1170 -- toe frame (_toe, _toe_in_ankle, home toe) drives waypoints, routes, turn rates and clearances; 946-955 tilt from _toe.basis.y; 1102 grip_offset 0.035+size.y*0.45; 1500, 1510, 1674-1677 tool frame from toe.basis.y
wako_pickup.gd:81, 94 -- grip.origin + grip.basis.y*0.035 contact test and foot anchor
wako_portable_gun.gd:87 -- gun grip frame from toe.basis and toe.basis.y*0.035

NOTE: with the flip both toe.basis.x and toe.basis.y are negated (Godot): every foot-held tool, gun control and cargo anchor built from the toe frame turns 180 deg about vertical until these consumers are retuned; the grip point (head + 0.035 along +Y, at y 0.095 / z 0.049) now lies about 2 cm inside the toe pad's front face (front of the foot at y 0.119 m)

runtime_benchmark.setup: 64 instances playing wk_run, identical untextured material, Godot 4.7.1 Forward+ on lavapipe (software Vulkan, 4 shared CPU threads), 640x360, frames 41-240, 2 interleaved runs per mesh while other jobs loaded the machine (load average ~35)
runtime_benchmark.note: noisy on a shared CPU (the same mesh varies 98-112 ms); after is ~10-15 % slower in this software-skinned setup (1484 vs 792 GPU vertices, 2550 vs 1110 triangles), which does not predict GPU cost. rev2 had 1450 GPU vertices / 2486 triangles.
